task.instructions: Experiment E2 (tests H12): CUTLASS 4.4 sm100 TF32 tcgen05 GEMM core: 2SM 256x256 tiles and W multicast, then the fused six-way bias epilogue (H13, H14). Two-file CUDA C++ layout (kernel.cu with CUTLASS, binding.cpp with torch glue); record build time, it must stay well under 300 s. Part A, GEMM core (tests H12/H13): with the Sm100 CollectiveBuilder (OpClassTensorOp, ElementA = ElementB = cutlass::tfloat32_t read straight from the fp32 pointers, ElementAccumulator float, A = emb [B,3072] K-major, B = W [18432,3072] K-major, D row-major [B,18432] fp32 into a tmp tensor, persistent tile scheduler, auto stage count), build and time at B = 5, 128, 384, 919 interleaved with cuBLAS TF32 (rented reference 50/51/74/135 us), 3 rounds: (i) 1SM KernelTmaWarpSpecialized1SmSm100, tile 128x256x32, cluster 1x1x1; (ii) 2SM KernelTmaWarpSpecialized2SmSm100, tile 256x256x32, cluster 2x1x1; (iii) 2SM with cluster 4x1x1 (W tile multicast across two pairs along M); (iv) 2SM tile 256x128x32 if 256x256 spills TMEM or smem stages drop below 3. Report TF/s and the tile/wave counts (M-tiles x 72 N-tiles over 148 SMs). Measure max |err| vs fp64 per B: tcgen05 truncates fp32 to tf32 while cuBLAS may round; if truncation exceeds 1.7e-3 at any B, add cvt.rna.tf32 rounding of the W/emb tiles before the MMA (in-smem transform) and re-measure. Part B, fused epilogue (H14): in order of preference, (a) CUTLASS grouped / ptr-array GEMM (pattern of examples/75_blackwell_grouped_gemm) with six problems M=B, N=3072, K=3072, per-group A offset c*3072*3072, per-group D pointer and per-group bias through the EVT per-column-bias fusion (problem sizes and pointer arrays passed in a device tensor built on the host via torch::empty + cudaMemcpyAsync is an extra activity, so prefer passing them as kernel arguments or in constant memory, or fill the device array inside the kernel's prologue from kernel arguments); (b) a custom epilogue functor/EVT node that maps global column n to (outs[n / 3072], n % 3072) with plain fp32 stores and adds bias[n] (3072 = 12 x 256 so the output pointer is uniform per 256-wide N-tile); (c) fallback: GEMM into tmp + scatter6 (2 launches) using the best Part A core. Correctness on all 16 x 10 rounds; exactly one launch for (a)/(b); include an S-band check that B = 5..128 run at <= 55 us (single M-tile, W streamed once). Success: Part A: 2SM 256x256 is >= 1.2x faster than 1SM 128x256 at B = 919 (H12 supported) and the best core is <= 115 us at 919 rented; cluster-4 multicast adds >= 5% at 919 (H13). Part B: one launch, 16/16 pass with max error <= 1.7e-3, <= 120 us at 919, <= 80 us at 449, <= 55 us at B <= 128 rented; predicted portal score >= 0.60. Refuted if: 2SM tiles are within 5% of 1SM at B = 919 (H12 refuted: not smem-bound; look at TMEM/stage limits or L2 instead) and cluster multicast changes 919 by < 3% (H13 refuted); or no CUTLASS configuration beats cuBLAS TF32 by more than 5% at any B (then the fused epilogue alone, worth 7-47 us, is the only gain and E1's batched path is the better vehicle). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Goal: bring every B <= 128 to 42-45 us rented and B=131-211 to <= 50 us, one launch, fp32 accumulate over the full K. Step 1 (time-box 1.5 h, the cheap test of the mechanism): in the r1 CUTLASS kernel, copy cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp (and its dispatch-policy tag) into the solution under a new class name, and pass TMA::CacheHintSm90::EVICT_FIRST to the A-operand (W) TMA loads via copy_atom.with(barrier, mcast_mask, cache_hint); rebind the builder's CollectiveOp template arguments to the new mainloop. Probe interleaved, 3 rounds, harness flush: 128x64x16-stage at B=5/16/32 and 256x64 / 256x192 / 256x256 at B=96/128/131/192/211, hinted vs unhinted. Also probe the unhinted 128x64 at B=5 with a read-based flush instead of zero_ to measure how much of its 51 us is the dirty-L2 penalty. Step 2: hand-written tcgen05 kernel for B <= 128 (then <= 256 if time): 144 CTAs x 1 SM, 128 W rows per CTA (chunk c = blockIdx*128/3072 uniform), producer warp issues cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d with .L2::cache_hint (createpolicy evict_first) for W boxes [128 rows x 32 k] fp32 with 128B swizzle into the canonical K-major SW128 UMMA layout, emb boxes [Bpad x 32 k] without hint; 6-7 stages (16 KB W + <= 16 KB emb each); tcgen05.alloc Bpad columns (N = B rounded up to 16, <= 128, or 256 for 129-256 with 1SM M=128); kind::tf32 UMMA M=128 N=Bpad K=8, four per stage, tcgen05.commit to the per-stage empty mbarrier; epilogue tcgen05.ld 32x32b by 4 warps (one TMEM lane quadrant each), add bias[m], store out_c[b*3072 + m - c*3072] coalesced over m. task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H19): Two-accumulator 2SM pair kernel for 256 < B <= 512: one pass over N = Bpad, judged in cycles against CUTLASS 256x192/256x256. Start from tc_pair.cu in r3-e2-tc-pair-kbs2 and keep tc_small (B <= 131) and the r3 pair (131 < B <= 256) exactly as they are. Build tc_pair2 for 256 < B <= 512: cluster of 2, cta_group::2, M = 256 W rows per pair, N1 = 256 and N2 = Bpad - 256 (Bpad = roundup(B, 16), so N2 is a multiple of 16 and N2/2 of 8) as two UMMAs per K = 8 step into two TMEM accumulators at columns [0, 256) and [256, Bpad); tcgen05.alloc 512 columns per CTA (1 CTA per SM by shared memory). Per CTA per k-block the shared memory holds 16 KB of W (its own 128 rows) and Bpad/2 emb rows laid out as 128 rows for UMMA1 (coordinate rank*128) followed by N2/2 rows for UMMA2 (coordinate 256 + rank*N2/2), loaded by two emb TMA boxes; the second B descriptor is the first plus 16 KB. Both idescs differ only in the N field; both accumulators' zero-init predicate uses the (i|j|k) != 0 rule per accumulator. Steps: (1) Probe first, in one container, cycles per k-block (clock64 span per CTA, %globaltimer for the clock) for kbs=1 with 3/4/5 stages at Bpad 384 and 464 and 3/4 stages at 512, plus kbs=2 with 2 stages, with real W from DRAM under the harness flush and evict_first on W; record MMA-ideal clk per k-block (2*128*Bpad*32/4096 per SM), the no-MMA feed-only time, and the resident-operand time for the same shapes, so each configuration is classified as MMA-, ingest- or chain-bound (H23/H24). (2) In the same probe run the CUTLASS tiles the kernel replaces (256x192 at 373/384, 256x256 at 449/512) and convert wall time x clock to cycles. (3) Ship the best configuration as the dispatch for 256 < B <= 512 (keep CUTLASS for B > 512), run_tests on all 16 workloads, record max |err| vs fp64 per B (must be <= 1.75e-3), and state the predicted portal time as max(1.05 x rented DRAM time, cycles / 1.55 GHz) plus the 11% underprediction seen at 192/211. Stretch only if the above is done: let the kernel take a batch-tile index (n0 offset in the emb coordinates and output columns) so E2 can reuse it; do not spend the session on L. Success: At 373/384/449/512 the kernel uses >= 20% fewer SM cycles than the CUTLASS tile it replaces in the same probe (target: <= 100k cycles at 384 and <= 125k at 512), passes 16/16 x 10 rounds with max |err| <= 1.75e-3, one launch, and the per-stage time at kbs=1 is within 15% of the MMA-ideal (chain floor hidden). Refuted if: The kbs=1 ring at N >= 384 still shows a per-stage time pinned near the 551-674 clk floor or above the MMA-ideal by more than 30% at every stage count, or cycles are within 10% of CUTLASS's at all four sizes. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

task.instructions: Experiment E3 (tests H26): 48-k stages (SW128 32-k + SW64 16-k boxes, 3-stage ring) for the two-accumulator pair at Bpad 384 and the nb2 L tiles. 1. Starting from r4-e1's tc_pair2 kernel (two accumulators, kbs1 ring), change the K stage from 32 to 48: per operand per stage two TMA loads, a 32-k box with 128B swizzle into a 1024-B-aligned region and a 16-k box with 64B swizzle into a separate region (W: 128 rows x 128 B + 128 rows x 64 B = 24 KB; emb: 192 rows at Bpad 384 = 36 KB; 60 KB per stage, 3 stages); K = 3072 = 64 stages; expect_tx covers both boxes of both operands (and the peer's bytes on the leader barrier as today). Build two UMMA smem descriptors per operand per stage: the SW128 one advanced by 32 B per K-step for K-steps 0-3 and an SW64 descriptor (SBO = 8 rows x 64 B = 512 B, swizzle mode 64B) advanced by 32 B for K-steps 4-5; 12 UMMAs per stage (6 K-steps x 2 accumulators), one commit per stage. Two TMA maps per operand (box 32-k SW128 and box 16-k SW64, both TFLOAT32 maps). 2. Validate numerically first at Bpad 384 against fp64 (max |err| <= 1.7e-3 on 3 draws, 0 elements outside atol+rtol) before timing; a wrong SW64 descriptor shows up as large errors, so also test a resident-operand unit test with known data. 3. Measure in one probe, interleaved, 3 rounds, with real W from DRAM and the harness flush: clk per 48-k stage and span at 373/384 for k48 st3 vs the r4-e1 kbs1 st4/st5 ring vs r4-e2 nb1, with the SM clock recorded; also try k48 with 2 stages (to show the 3-stage requirement) and kbs1 st4 as control in the same container. 4. If k48 wins at 384 by >= 10% in cycles, apply the same stage to r4-e2's nb2 kernel at Ntile 352/400/432 (691/773/853: emb 176/200/216 rows per CTA = 33-40.5 KB + 24 KB W; 3 stages fit) and to nb1 at Bpad 464 (67.5 KB x 3), and measure the same way against the r4-e2 nb2 ring and CUTLASS. 5. Ship the result as a candidate with dispatch: k48 at the B's where it wins by >= 5% in cycles, everything else as in r4-e1 (B <= 131 unchanged); run_tests 16/16, one launch, max |err| per B. Success: At 373/384: per-stage time <= 1.15 x 1152 clk (span <= 90k clk vs 107-111k for r4-e1, i.e. >= -15% in cycles at the same clock) and run_tests 16/16; a portal prediction of <= 68 us at 373/384 (vs 83); bonus if nb2 at 691-853 drops >= 10% in cycles Refuted if: The k48 3-stage ring with DRAM W runs >= 1350 clk per stage at Bpad 384 (latency-bound with 3 x 60 KB, i.e. no better than 950 per 32-k), or the SW64 descriptor path makes the UMMAs slower than the SW128 path (resident-operand k48 stage > 1250 clk), or the fixed cost of two TMA boxes per operand raises the feed-only per-stage time above 1100 clk This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).
